str: Markers Used in References for Airplane Flights Report
Allows the entry of flight time flown in actual IMC.
Additional ratings: aerobatic rating, flight test rating, en route instrument rating (EIR), mountain rating, night rating, sailplane and banner towing ratings, cloud flying
Acquisition of aerobatic privilege in the specified aircraft category.
Tracking of aerobatic flights. Aerobatic rating privileges are limited to the aircraft category in which the flight instruction was completed.
Allows the entry of flight time that is assigned to agricultural activities.
Allows the entry of flight time that is spent on airborne laser scanning based on LiDAR technology.
Examination by a qualified examiner for an instructor certificate.
The type of approach for the flight.
Tracking of reduced flight time, meaning actual time on controls, for CMD and FO in augmented crew operations.
Tracking of number of banner tows. A minimum of 5 tows during the last 24 months is required to keep the privileges of a banner towing rating.
A bird strike took place on the flight.
Allows the entry of flight time during which a mounted camera was operated.
Cargo weight (in kg) which was carried on the flight.
Allows the entry of flight time during which cloud seeding operations were performed.
The names of other crew members on the flight.
A flight between a point of departure and a point of arrival following a preplanned route, using standard navigation procedures.
Allows to mark flights with routes that cross actual sea terrain.
Completion of training courses or familiarization courses for aircraft types, license, and ratings privileges.
Track flights with de-icing operations performed, including the application of de-icing or anti-icing fluids to ensure safe flight operations in adverse weather conditions.
Flight instructor applicant observed by examiner while training student(s).
Marks part of difference training requiring the acquisition of additional knowledge and training - on appropriate training device or aircraft - in order to gain privileges on
another class or variant of airplane/helicopter.
Training conducted under the EASA Evidence Based Training (EBT) programme. The EVAL/MVP marker shall only be set in the case of a 'competent' outcome,
where no competency has been assessed below level 2. This marker is used for cross-credit towards revalidation of other class and type ratings. Typically, the EVAL
phase takes place on day 1. The marker may also be set if the competency grades are successfully reworked afterwards.
Tracking of time and number of flights as examiner for the purpose of revalidation or renewal of examiner certificate.
Part of the revalidation procedure for a class or type rating when less than 10 route sectors have been flown in the corresponding class or type.
Marks part of familiarization training requiring the acquisition of additional knowledge to gain privileges for a different class or variant of the airplane/helicopter than the
one used for the skill test of the licence.
Tracking of flights conducted for the purpose of positioning an aircraft, typically without passengers or cargo, to or from a specific location, often for maintenance,
Tracking of flights during which the privileges of an FI to conduct flight instruction for the issue, revalidation or renewal of an FI, IRI, CRI, STI or an MI certificate are
Allows the entry of flight time that is assigned to firefighting.
The flight number of the conducted flight.
Tracking of test flights as PIC in category 1 or 2 according to the privileges held.
Tracking of landings on glaciers, requiring specialized techniques, equipment, and training to ensure safe aircraft handling on snow or ice surfaces.
Tracking of takeoffs from glaciers, requiring specialized techniques, equipment, and training to ensure safe aircraft handling on snow or ice surfaces.
Allows the entry of flight time that is assigned to infrastructure related activities.
Any aircraft training that involves landing the aircraft under instruction or observation of an instructor.
Tracking of tests given as language assessor.
Communication assessment required every 4 years (operational level) or every 6 years (extended level) for target language. For holders of IR and EIR ratings,
proficiency in English at operational or extended level is required.
Allows the entry of flight time during which the left seat in multi crew operations is occupied.
The lesson (part of the syllabus) instructed on the flight or simulator session.
